title: Behavioural exercise model for §489 and Bauspar optionality
summary: An open project: replace the deterministic exercise boundary in the hedge model with a conditional exercise intensity, without discarding the rational frontier. The target architecture runs curve, rational exercise value, behavioural hazard, survival, expected cash flows, PV and DV01, hedge — in place of the current curve, threshold, terminate or stay, hedge. The threshold is not removed; it becomes the incentive variable that drives the hazard.
friction: Review of the first draft surfaced the obstacle that decides whether this project is tractable: a hazard fitted to observed borrower behaviour is a real-world probability, while the swaption valuation is risk-neutral. Substituting the first into the second is not automatic, and no correction has been chosen.

The first framing treated behavioural deviation as replacing the rational-exercise rule. That was too strong. §489 is the borrower's right, so failure to exercise costs the lender less; optimal exercise is the conservative bound and the threshold survives as the main explanatory variable of exercise intensity rather than as the exercise law.
notes:
The exported project carries a description and no documents; nothing has been built, so evidence stays empty. Design decisions recorded from review of the draft post, not from work done:
- Model the exercise time as a conditional intensity P(tau = t | tau >= t, F_t) rather than as the stopping time inf{t : F_t < K}.
- Drive the hazard by the refinancing incentive I = K - F_t, the coupon against the competing forward, plus borrower and contract characteristics.
- Prefer discrete-time survival for monthly Bauspar and loan data over a continuous-time proportional-hazards fit; a logit link on the period hazard is the natural first form.
- Treat a contract still running at the observation cut as right-censored, not as a non-event: observed duration is min(T, T_obs) with an indicator for whether the event was seen.
- Once cash flows depend on the exercise time, the hedge faces a distribution of profiles rather than one profile, so DV01 is an expectation and not a single number.
The measure mismatch recorded in friction gates all of this and is unresolved.
